newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends unchanged after employment data.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends unchanged after employment data.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended mostly unchanged on Friday from opening levels around C$1.3690 (US$0.7305) after Canada and the United States reported February employment data.
* Dealers said Canada's dollar remained pressured by jitters over possible U.S. rate rises and Canadian job losses in February.

Traders said speculation had grown that the Federal Reserve might raise U.S. interest rates after the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in the wake of news that U.S. non-farm payrolls rose 339,000, far more than Wall Street had expected.

"Headline figures like these are going to keep the Bank of Canada holding fast for a while and, with (Federal Reserve chairman) Mr. (Alan) Greenspan set to pull the trigger soon, I would suggest long the Canadian dollar is not where you want to be," said David Rosenberg, economist at Nesbitt Burns in Toronto.
In Canadian economic news, Statistics Canada reported the nation lost 38,000 full-time jobs in February, worse than analysts' expectations.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 1.2505 marks from Thursday's close at 1.2572 marks but rose to 89.04 yen from Thursday's close of 88.67 yen.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
